speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether the Government will be studying the feasibility of establishing a new body to regulate artificial intelligence (AI) in Singapore; and (b) what are the efforts made in working with other governments to coordinate responsible development and deployment of AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our governance approach is a practical and risk-based one, as explained at the Sittings of 21 April 2023 and 9 May 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: AI is fast becoming a general-purpose technology that is applied across many sectors and use cases.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We cannot and should not adopt a one-size-fits-all approach to regulate it, nor is it realistic to address in advance every risk out there.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nonetheless, the Government hopes to see AI deployed in a responsible and ethical way, aligned with international norms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) have several initiatives to guide the development and deployment of AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA has open-sourced AI Verify, an AI governance testing framework and software toolkit.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It strengthens trust by enabling objective validation of a company’s implementation of responsible AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is, however, a minimum viable product that we hope will grow over time.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These initiatives have been noticed and commended by our international and industry partners as practical steps for thinking about how responsible AI developments can be implemented.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to monitor developments and are prepared to adjust our implementation approach as knowledge and understanding evolves.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: AI governance is also an area that benefits from more international cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In this regard, Singapore is engaging widely with our international partners through multilateral platforms, such as the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, we are engaging other like-minded partners, such as Israel, the Republic of Korea and the UK, with whom we have signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) to cooperate on AI and emerging technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the US, we have been partnering their National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to advance our alignment on AI governance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I understand that it may be quite difficult to legislate AI altogether, especially as it might inevitably hamper innovation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But I am wondering whether there would be continuous effort to look at more upstream factors so that we can better control and mitigate any impact there may be in generations to come.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I can give an analogy, when I am asked this question about AI governance, there is no doubt it is happening very quickly and we will see accelerated deployments potentially across many different sectors, but it still takes time to understand fully how the risks present themselves and what to do about moderating these risks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The automobile industry is a very good example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When cars were first made available, their reach was not very wide.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would probably be the same for AI deployment, too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: AI, for example, takes a lot of compute power, so, it is not cheap to implement AI systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As such, the early implementations will still take time to present themselves.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But going back to the example of automotives, it was not immediately obvious to people that what helps to prevent deaths and injuries in a motor vehicle accident would be something like a seat belt.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And subsequent to seat belts, then people figured out that having an air bag is quite useful, too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But these kinds of measures, they do not present themselves at the outset.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not really know what will work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It takes research, it takes a lot of exchange of knowledge and understanding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And then, after a while, we figured out that maybe, seat belts should be made a requirement; maybe air bags should be required as well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would also say that using automotives as an example, it is not just the thing itself, the device itself, the equipment itself, that can have safety features built in.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In order to promote road safety, actually, human society figured out that traffic lights are important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We figured out that speed limits are important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But you do not need the same speed limits on highways versus country roads.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And then, we figured out that, okay, if you had an ageing population, vulnerable segments of the population, you can do a Silver Zone – well, that is what we do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Keep in mind that we cannot operate only on the basis of domestic interests.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Otherwise, our businesses will find it very difficult to meet the requirements when they operate in different jurisdictions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The approach that we take in Singapore is to try our best to be plugged into as many of these conversations as possible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will not be the only ones thinking about governance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The more we share with our international counterparts, the more we are able to look over the horizon and take steps to raise our own regulatory measures in accordance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The way in which we have introduced regulations for online media, for example, how do we look after safety issues, how do we tackle criminal harms that are being carried out online – and yesterday's new legislation is a good example of this.
